title: East St. Louis Toodle-oo as theme
summary: On the 1930 session Cootie played plunger on the Ellington theme song East St. Louis; they note A Train replaced it.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. Let's hold it a minute now.
Cootie, on that same session, you made "East St. Louis". So you were featured on that, too.
Oh, yeah. "East St. Louis" Tadd's-00. (Unintelligible)
Well, that was the theme song.
Because that was the theme.
Yeah.
Wasn't it.
That was the theme song.
Well, so, on that theme, did that get played like a chorus and then on the second chorus you were featured? Can you remember?
No.
Or were you playing plunger right from the start, in that first chorus?
Right in the first chorus.
Oh, you were. Yeah.
All the way to the end.
All the way to the end.
Yeah. All the way to the end.
Yeah. When -- was that -- where did that number come from? I've forgotten. Did Duke write all of that?
I wasn't there.
Maybe he wrote it with Bubber.
Yeah. Maybe Bubber.
I should think so, wouldn't you?
Yeah.
That was probably the real early days in the Kentucky Club or something, where they were -- where Bubber supplied something, and they made it their theme. When it was real -- just the few guys.
Yeah.
The five or six guys or whatever.
Yeah.
It's a beautiful thing. Don't you think it is?
Yeah. I liked it very much.
I always was sorry that he ever did change that theme. But still, you know -- well, not only did he use "A Train" for a theme, but he used --
That was the only two I remembered.
Was it?
That I recall, yeah.
There wasn't one between "A Train", then.
No.
Oh. So he never switched until Strayhorn was in the band then.
That's right.
